The Use Case model is a catalogue of system functionality described using UML Use Cases. Each Use Case represents a single, repeatable interaction that a user or "actor" experiences when using the system.
A Use Case typically includes one or more "scenarios" which describe the interactions that go on between the Actor and the System, and documents the results and exceptions that occur from the user's perspective.
Use Cases may include other Use Cases as part of a larger pattern of interaction and may also be extended by other use cases to handle exceptional conditions

This package contains use cases which define how an Actor will interact with the proposed system.
Each interaction may be specified using scenarios, sequence diagrams, communication diagrams and other dynamic diagrams or textual descriptions which together how the system when viewed as a "black-box" interacts with a user.

Actors are the users of the system being modeled. Each Actor will have a well-defined role, and in the context of that role have useful interactions with the system.
A person may perform the role of more than one Actor, although they will only assume one role during one use case interaction.
An Actor role may be performed by a non-human system, such as another computer program.
The System Boundary shows the logical interface between users and the system being described.

The Domain Model is a view of all the objects that make up an area of interest, and their relationships. It is used to capture the significant objects within a system, organization or any target domain.
The Domain class model captures essential information about objects in the domain.

Map a numerical time format (e.g UNIX time) into SDMX. Example: UNIX Time basePeriod: 1970-01-01 targetFrequencyId : A epochPeriod : millisecond The output Frequency could be derived from the reported value in the FREQ dimension. Where the reported FREQ is not a SDMX frequency or a Frequency that can have 2 output formats e.g. Monthly 2009-01 or 2009-M01 the mappedFrequencies can be used to define Id to pattern

A ComponentMap maps one or more source Dimensions/Attributes to one or more target Dimensions/Attributes or a fixed value.
The way the values map (e.g UK maps to GBP or $ maps to USD or A2007 maps to 2007) is derived from the rules described in the RepresentationMap or for Date types EpochMapping/DatePatternMapping. It can only reference one of these mapping types.

Whilst these classes are abstract the agency/id/version is sufficient to enable the identification of the scheme type and so the individual schemes do not have individual classes to structure the mapping.

Map one or more date patterns to either a target frequency id OR to a frequency dimension which is used to convert the date. Example: Convert date to the frequency id reported against the FREQ Dimension frequencyDimension = FREQ sourcePattern = DD/MM/YYYY locale = fr-FR Example: Convert each date format to a specific frequency depending on the source format of the date. Two Date Mappings are defined, one for daily data, one for Quarterly where the source data uses a different date pattern for each targetFrequencyId= D sourcePattern = DD/MM/YYYY targetFrequencyId= Q sourcePattern = YYYYQn

This enables any type of Scheme to be mapped to a different Scheme type e.g. Category Scheme to Data Provider.
The original note gave the e.g. as Code List to Data Provider, but the Code List Map is not a sub class of Item Scheme Map any more
At V 2.1 the mapping is restricted to the source and target being of the same Scheme Type. This was modeled at level of the item (e.g. a Concept references a Concept Scheme Map). So perhaps this should be retained

RepresentationMap is used to define the rules on how source value(s) map to target value(s) for 1 mapping in a StructureMap. For example if the Dimension COUNTRY maps to REF_AREA then the RepresentationMap contains the rules for how the two underlying Codelist values map (USA maps to US).
As the StructureMap can define a single mapping as 1..n sources mapping 1..n targets, the sources and targets in a RepresentationMap are also 1..n to mirror the cardinality of the mapped Components. For example COUNTRY+AGE+CURRENCY maps to INDICATOR. In this example the combination of reported value for 3 Dimensions map to a single INDICATOR. As each Dimension has a different representation (COUNTRY=Codelist, Age=Integer, CURRENCY=ValueList) the sources comprise of a reference to a Codelist, Integer, and ValueList.

Multiple source values can map to zero or more targets. There should be a source value for each source ValueRepresentation. For example if the source ValueRepresentations are REF_AREA + AGE, UK could be one mapped value (REF_AREA) and 16 could be another (for AGE). The source values can be pattern matched by using regular expressions, or match on a substring by using start/end index. For example UK_BNK could match the MappedValue UK if the endIndex is set to 2 (only take the first 2 characters from UK_BNK to match) The target value(s) is always an a absolute string however if the MappedValue is a regular expression, the target value can output the capture group from the source. Example: Mapped Value is regular expression MappedValue: source=A([0-9]{4}) TargetValue: \1-01-01 The input A2009 would output 2009-01-01 as 2009 is matched by the first regular expression capture group, and output in the target in place of \1
Source and target must be of the same type (Either Data Structure to Data Structure or Dataflow to Dataflow)
The concrete classes in the ItemSchemeAssociation restrict the mapping to schemes and items of the same type (e.g. a code list and its code must be mapped to another code list and its codes).
Optional information to describe how frequency code ids map to the output format. Example frequencyId =A1 datePattern=YYYY frequencyId =M1 datePattern=YYYY-MM
Describes how reported values map, can support multiple sources/targets which are represented by different types (e.g Codelists, Value List or facet such as Integer).
Source and target must be of the same type (Either Data Structure to Data Structure or Dataflow to Dataflow)
The process step can reference any identifiable object as input or output.
This is registry based metadata

The Connections package models the dependencies and connectivity between the various components, and how each is used as part of a co-operative system to accomplish required tasks. Typically, Components expose interfaces and API's which are used by other Components.

The Component Model defines how classes, artifacts and other low level elements are collected into high level components and the interfaces and connections between them.
Components are compiled software artifacts that work together to provide the required behavior within the operating constraints defined in the requirements model. Components will generally be deployed to varying hardware platforms described in the Deployment Model.

The Components package contains modeled components and their structural constituents. These include additional exposed interfaces, ports and other gateways or internal structural components.
The connectivity and internal structure of these are further modeled in the Internal Structures and Connections packages

Internal Structures provide a detailed view of the internal workings and dependencies of a component. Using a Composite Structure diagram, they illustrate how the component fulfills its behavioral contracts and provides interface behavior to other components within the system.
This component exposes an interface for other components to use. The interface is a contract to provide specific behavior to other components that require that service.

The Connections package contains detailed wiring diagrams of the explicit connections established between components at run-time.
Typically this is shown as a dependency relationship between a required interface on one component being connected to a provided interface on a second component. These dependency relationships show how each components requirements for functionality are met by other components, and how the system as a whole is capable of performing the required work.
This component needs the services of another component to perform its required work.
This illustrates how the services offered by this component are internally delegated to a specific object.

The Internal Structures package contains models of how components are internally wired to provide both internal and external services. These composite structure diagrams detail the connections and dependencies within components, usually between classes (objects or parts) and supported interfaces (services).
